title: Participant-Average Effects in Cluster Trials with Heavy-Tailed Pareto Cluster Sizes
banked_reason: D0.5.G: tier=subfield < floor=field, paper_score_ceiling=7.2 < ceiling_for_field=7.4, salvageable=false; math review passes and the cited source is verified.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

The delivered result is an order-sharp honest-confidence-length frontier on two same-class constructions, but its significance is limited by the exact known discrete-Pareto size law and the strong bespoke conditional-Wasserstein alignment structure used to cancel tail bias.

The unrestricted-onset result covers only two known contraction exponents and its feasible interval still uses the known slower exponent, so it establishes a specific onset obstruction rather than broad adaptation to unknown heavy-tail structure.
The critical Hájek theorem is only pointwise and unstudentized, and its computed tail constant is not an exact minimax confidence-length constant or a directly usable uniform inference procedure.

The matched fixed-onset frontier is a plausible contribution, but its Peng/Brahimi positioning only says that their marginal-tail models and targets differ; it must state the closest theorem-level assumptions, interval/loss conclusion, and the precise reason neither supplies this uniform same-class minimax rate.

The unrestricted-onset frontier is positioned only against generic adaptation context; identify and compare the closest adaptation-confidence result(s), distinguishing unknown onset/contraction from unknown tail parameters and stating exactly what their guarantees do not cover.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching honest expected-length upper and lower rates on the specified fixed-onset Pareto/conditional-mark class and a matched unrestricted-onset frontier; it also derived a pointwise critical Hájek CLT with explicit tail constants. D0.5 mathematical review passed with no findings and verified the cited normal-domain criterion, but the independent novelty review placed the delivered package at subfield below the mandated field floor. The two unrepaired panel findings concern second-order heavy-mean and adaptation-confidence positioning; they were not the reason for the below-floor halt. No Lean formalization was started.
tldr: For the participant-average effect under the known exact discrete Pareto size law, the bespoke fixed-onset conditional-mark class \(F\) has a proved three-regime order frontier for honest expected confidence length: \(G^{-(\alpha+\gamma+\rho-1)/(\alpha+2\rho)}\) in the stable regime, \(\sqrt{\log G/G}\) at the critical boundary, and \(G^{-1/2}\) in the Gaussian regime. Separately, at the critical boundary the raw participant-weighted Hajek estimator has the pointwise limit \(\sqrt{G/\log G}(\widehat\tau_H-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,(K_++K_-)/m(P)^2)\); the same theorem evaluates its smooth-base variance as \(c^2/\{7p(1-p)m(P_0)^2\}\). Over the distinct unrestricted-onset union \(E\), the matched honest-length frontier is \(G^{-(\alpha+\gamma_L-1)/\alpha}\). The pointwise critical CLT is neither a uniform Studentized result nor an exact minimax confidence-length constant.
gap: Published CRT inference defines the participant-weighted target but its cited size-moment assumption excludes the exact Pareto law here. Heavy-score resampling and second-order heavy-mean inference do not establish the honest-length frontier on one conditional-mark causal class.
fill: Establish finite-sample honest upper bounds, matching testing lower bounds in stable, critical, and Gaussian regimes, and a separate sharp rate obstruction over an unrestricted-onset union.
